purpose: Test whether two independently controllable facts fuse/fission during computation; dual methodology (opaque transplants + R^n cosine)

metrics.breakpoint: cosine ~1.0 at layers where transplant behavior differs dramatically

notes: PHASE 2 FIRST DATA POINT. 12 transitions detected. Critical breakpoint: R^n cosine sees all worlds as identical (~1.0) at layers where transplants show FUSED vs SEPARATE behavior. Native compositional structure invisible to R^n global distance. Caveats: baseline only 75% (2/8 wrong), single prompt template, binary values only.

purpose: PCA probe: can linear subspace find compositional structure that global cosine misses?
notes: PCA SEPARATES at all layers. Structure is low-rank linear. But PCA separation does not predict behavioral fusion/fission. Key finding: PRESENCE (PCA decode) != ADDRESSABILITY (transplant control). Facts linearly decodable even when behaviorally inseparable. Confirms BP-1, strengthens BP-9. A>B asymmetry: A-sep ~13x B-sep at late layers.

purpose: Attention analysis: does cross-fact attention predict behavioral fusion?
notes: Fusion is NOT attention-mediated. Cross-fact attention is slightly LOWER at fused layers. Last token overwhelmingly attends to fact A (HESK) over fact B (VORN), explaining the A>B PCA asymmetry. The fusion mechanism must be in the MLP or residual stream, not attention.

purpose: Component-level transplant: is fusion in attention, MLP, or the whole state?
notes: NEITHER attention-only NOR MLP-only transplant can flip fact B. Full transplant shifts B by +4.1 logits but each component alone shifts by at most ~1.1. Fusion is a WHOLE-STATE property of the residual stream, not localizable to any single transformer component. Confirms BP-2 (distributed state). Caveat: full transplant flips B at ALL layers including SEPARATE because donor model answers B incorrectly in World 10.

purpose: Trajectory analysis: do world trajectories converge at fused layers?
notes: Worlds ALWAYS diverge (never converge). FUSED layers diverge slowly (-1.2), SEPARATE layers diverge fast (-5.7). Fusion = world-insensitive computation. Fission = world-sensitive computation. Static trajectory metrics are too coarse — the behavioral transplant amplifies tiny directional differences through remaining layers. Native math must model SENSITIVITY TO PERTURBATION across layers, not just state geometry.

purpose: Fix BPE boundary token mismatch in v2 transplant instrument — donor now runs on full prompt (not storage-only) to ensure identical tokenization. Self-patch should be exactly zero.
notes: BPE fix confirmed: self-patch exactly zero across all configs. Root cause was tokenizer merging final period with newline into a single token when followed by query. Fix: run donor on full prompt (not storage-only). ZOG/MIP shows 25 PARTIAL layers (strong causal transfer, K[1][1] grows to 1.50), HESK/VORN all NO_CONTROL. purpose: Test behavioral distance (next-token KL/JSD) vs R^n distance (cosine) for four fact-worlds. Behavioral distance is a proper metric (sqrt(JSD)), correctly reflects factual structure (same-fact worlds 2.35x closer), KL is asymmetric (1.7x ratio), and cosine INVERTS the ranking at early layers.
notes: First genuinely behavioral (non-R^n) measurement. sqrt(JSD) forms proper metric. Cosine inverts fact-relevance ranking at layer 0 (w00-w10 closer than w00-w01 by cosine, but 3.5x farther by behavioral KL). KL asymmetry supports BP-3 (native distance may be asymmetric). Next: layer-dependent behavioral distance to find where the model first separates facts.

purpose: Layer-dependent behavioral distance via logit lens — does the model have a resolution layer where it selects the queried fact and suppresses the irrelevant one?
notes: First clean replicating non-R^n finding. Logit lens (final norm+unembedding applied at each layer) + JSD measures query-selective resolution: at layer 25, model amplifies queried fact behavioral signature (JSD 0.72-0.80) while suppressing irrelevant fact (JSD 0.01-0.11). Cosine stays 0.91-0.99 throughout. Replicates across 3 entity pairs x 2 query targets x 2 templates = 6 configs. HESK/VORN peaks earlier (L21). T3 template peaks later (L26) with weaker amplitude. Independent of K-matrix instrument (no transplants).

purpose: Test whether Qwen3-0.6B supports a product-of-registers overwrite algebra via purely behavioral (no hooks/vectors) token-level setter and query operations
notes: FAIL: product-of-registers algebra not supported. 16 types instead of 4 (presentation entanglement). Last-write-wins at 27% (model has primacy bias - first mention dominates over later contradictory setters). Disjoint commutation at 56%. The model cannot reliably overwrite facts via in-context appending. This tells us that the model is not a clean register machine at the behavioral level. The primacy bias is a structural property: early tokens establish a world model that later tokens cannot easily override. This connects to the logit-lens resolution finding (resolution layer at L21-25 establishes which fact the model will use). Genuine non-R^n data: no vectors touched.

purpose: Test whether attention routing explains logit-lens resolution layer. Measures attention from query position to queried vs irrelevant entity tokens across all layers, compares to JSD ratio.
notes: PASS (confound ruled out): attention ratio does NOT explain JSD ratio. Correlation range -0.10 to +0.25, all well below 0.7 kill threshold. Attention to queried entity is already HIGH from L3 onward (~0.5-0.8 across ALL layers, not selective). JSD ratio spikes at L21-25 WITHOUT corresponding attention spike. QueryB case especially clear: attention ratio near 0 everywhere (KROT is second in prompt) yet JSD ratio peaks 62.43x at L24-25. The resolution layer finding is NOT reducible to attention routing. Something in the MLP/combined transformation creates selective amplification independent of attention weights.

purpose: Decompose resolution into attention vs MLP: hook post-attention (before MLP) and post-MLP states, apply logit lens, compare JSD ratios.
notes: SURPRISING: Resolution is already present AFTER attention, BEFORE the MLP. The attention WEIGHTS are not selective (attention_control_v1 showed r~0), but the attention OUTPUT is — meaning the resolution is in the VALUE space, not the key/query routing. The MLP modulates rather than creates the resolution: sometimes sharpens (+8.61 for HESK/VORN) and sometimes blurs (-15.46 for PLIM/KROT). The resolution is an emergent property of value-vector composition at resolution layers.

purpose: Test whether resolution layer generalizes to 3-fact worlds (3 entities × 2 values each = 8 worlds). Does the model suppress BOTH irrelevant facts simultaneously?
notes: Resolution generalizes to 3-fact worlds. All configs with clean baselines show resolution at L25 with ratios 10-42x. BOTH irrelevant facts are suppressed simultaneously and equally (HESK/VORN/KROT: irrel1=0.0195, irrel2=0.0194). Resolution strength correlates with baseline accuracy (4/4 → 10-42x; 2/4 → 1.7x). The last entity (PLIM queryC) resolves just as cleanly (28.59x) as the first, so the mechanism is not simply primacy. This is a general mechanism, not pairwise competition.

purpose: Causal test: inject query-A hidden state into query-B forward pass at each layer. Tests whether resolution layer is causally active.
notes: UNINFORMATIVE: full-state injection at ANY layer carries donor information through all remaining layers, producing identical logits regardless of injection point. This tells us the fact-identity signal is present at ALL layers (not created at L25) — the resolution layer AMPLIFIES an already-present signal, it does not create it. A meaningful causal test needs partial-state injection (targeted subspace patching), which requires R^n tools. The correlational logit-lens evidence (5 experiments) is the stronger proof path for now.

purpose: Test whether continuations produce the same DISTRIBUTION (not just greedy answer) across same-place histories. Strengthens continuation_congruence_v1 from argmax equality to full next-token distribution equality via sqrt(JSD).
notes: 100% DEFECT RATE at distributional level despite 97% greedy congruence. Same-place histories (identical greedy answers) produce SUBSTANTIALLY DIFFERENT full next-token distributions (JSD 0.07-0.45). Greedy congruence was lucky argmax agreement, not distributional identity. Repeat-ZOG continuations show lowest divergence (avg 0.168), corrections highest (0.275). The behavioral place defined by greedy answers is COARSER than the model's actual internal state. The native mathematics needs finer-grained equivalence classes.

purpose: Measure how output distribution entropy evolves across layers via logit lens. Connect resolution layer to distributional congruence failure.
notes: COMMITMENT BOTTLENECK: entropy drops to near-zero at L24-25 (0.05-0.30 bits, top-1 mass 0.99+) then JUMPS BACK UP to 5.5-7.7 bits in the final output. The model commits at L25 (near-certain of the answer) then re-broadens the distribution in the final layers. The argmax survives re-broadening but the distributional tails change. This explains the distributional congruence failure: the commitment bottleneck makes greedy answers congruent across histories, but the re-broadening re-injects history-dependent distributional structure.

purpose: Test whether the re-broadened final distribution carries meaningful history information or generic noise. Also investigate L27 vs final-output entropy discrepancy.

metrics.detail: Top divergent tokens between same-place histories are overwhelmingly history-related (entity values, variant capitalization). 5-7 of top 10 divergent tokens are fact-world values.
metrics.entropy_std_vs_dup: dup consistently 2-3x lower (ZOG: 2.17 vs 5.86; MIP: 2.99 vs 7.66; PLIM: 2.28 vs 5.94)

notes: Two findings: (1) The re-broadened distribution is MEANINGFUL, not noise. The model leaks information about the ENTIRE fact-world into every output position's distribution, not just the queried fact. Divergent tokens between same-place histories are dominated by entity values (big/small/hot/cold/red/blue) and their capitalizations. (2) Repetition narrows the distribution: dup variants have 2-3x lower entropy than std/rev. Connects to primacy bias. (3) L27 logit-lens vs final output JSD=0.356, entropy 1.27 vs 5.86 — substantial discrepancy suggesting the final norm+lm_head interacts non-trivially with the hidden state at the last layer.

purpose: Codex-directed (v4): test whether distributional residual inside greedy fibers is predictive state or presentation leakage. Three pair classes, six continuations.
notes: MIXED RESULT: The distributional residual inside greedy fibers is BOTH predictive and presentation leakage. At baseline (empty) and after corrections: history>benign (3/3), meaning the residual is task-relevant predictive state — corrections interact differently with different histories. After neutral continuations and canonical restatement: history<benign (0/3), meaning the residual is partially resetable presentation structure. Cross-world distance is SMALLEST everywhere — presentation matters more than irrelevant fact content. The canonical restatement acts as a partial SYNCHRONIZATION operation, reducing all within-fiber distances. The native algebra has both a predictive commitment component and a resetable presentation component.
